# The vendored libraries and their two path bootstraps

> Trigger: read this when you touch `sys.path`, the vendored `thehive4py`/`cortex4py`, or a local patch.

### Two path bootstraps, only one of which finds the vendored libraries

`thehive4py` and `cortex4py` live in `package/bin/ta_thehive_cortex/libs/`, a
directory Python knows nothing about until something puts it on `sys.path`.
There are two bootstraps and they are **not** equivalent:

* `ta_thehive_cortex_declare` (ours) adds `lib/`, `bin/ta_thehive_cortex/` and
  `bin/ta_thehive_cortex/libs/`;
* `import_declare_test` (generated by `ucc-gen`) adds `lib/` and
  `bin/TA-thehive-cortex` -- note the capitals, a directory that does not
  exist. It knows nothing of the vendored libraries.

`thehive_observables.py` and `backfill_observables.py` used the second one and
import `thehive4py` a dozen lines below. Measured: with only `bin/` on the
path, `thehive4py` does not resolve. They worked **by accident** -- an earlier
`from thehive import …` fixes `sys.path` as a SIDE EFFECT, before the line that
needs it runs.

⚠️ That is a trap, not a design, and it is armed by the most routine action
there is: **reordering imports**. Every linter does it, and the resulting
`ModuleNotFoundError` names the library rather than the reordering, sending the
reader to look at vendoring instead of at import order.

⚠️ It also nearly produced the wrong fix. `import_declare_test` looks like an
unused import -- nothing references the name -- so an unused-import sweep would
have DELETED it, breaking the modules outright instead of leaving them fragile.
A side-effect import is never unused; check what an import *does* before
concluding it does nothing.

### A green suite proves the paths it RUNS, and nothing about the rest

The sharpest lesson of the refactor, and it was self-inflicted. Extracting the
shared bootstrap left `modalert_args.py` importing `create_thehive_instance`
from `modalert_thehive_common`, which does not define it -- the function lives
in `thehive`. That is an `ImportError` on the first useful line of **both**
creation alert actions: `thehive_create_a_new_case` and
`thehive_create_a_new_alert`, dead on arrival.

**123 tests were green.** Not one of them entered the extracted function, so
the suite was structurally unable to see it. The failure is not that a test was
weak; it is that a new function shipped with **no** test executing it, and a
suite cannot report on a path it never takes.

Two guards now cover the two halves:

* `tools/checks/local_imports_resolve.py` -- static, so it needs neither Splunk
  nor solnlib: every `from <local module> import <name>` must name something
  that module defines. It reports where the name actually lives, which turns a
  five-minute hunt into a one-line fix.
* a test that **executes** `prepare_instances` with a stand-in helper, so the
  lazy import is really performed. ⚠️ Note the shape: the modules are replaced
  in `sys.modules` rather than the function patched, precisely so the import
  statement runs. Patching the function would have kept the test green.

⚠️ Rule of thumb from this: **when you extract a function, write the test that
calls it before you write anything else.** An extraction moves code out of the
paths the suite already covers, so the moment of extraction is exactly the
moment coverage silently drops.

## R44 — Cortex is reached through `cortex4py`, and through nothing else

**Decision.** Every call to Cortex goes through the vendored `cortex4py`. The
`thehive4py` route to Cortex -- `libs/thehive4py/endpoints/cortex.py`, with
`create_analyzer_job`, `create_responder_action`, `list_analyzers` and
`list_responders` -- is **written off**. It has zero call sites today, and it
keeps zero.

**Why.** It would be a second way to do one gesture: two code paths, two
behaviours to explain when they disagree, two surfaces to maintain, and a
Cortex instance addressed sometimes directly and sometimes through TheHive.
The `cortex4py` route is the one this add-on already configures, authenticates
and logs.

**The consequence, stated rather than discovered.** Cortex **responders** stay
out of reach. They are not merely unimplemented here: `cortex4py` has no
responder controller at all, so the direct route cannot express them. Anyone
wanting responders is choosing to reopen this decision, not to add a feature on
top of it.

## A method the library has and nobody calls is a signal, not a curiosity

Two of the three defects behind `cortexjobs` were exactly that shape:
`jobs.get_report_async()` (Cortex holds the answer server-side, instead of us
asking too early) and `jobs.get_artifacts()` (the observables an analyzer
extracts) sat in the vendored library, fully working, with **zero** call sites.
The enrichment Cortex produced never came back to Splunk -- not because of a
bug, but because nobody had ever compared the two lists.

So compare them, as a periodic review gesture rather than an accident:

```bash
# what the library offers
grep -rn "    def [a-z]" TA-thehive-cortex/package/bin/ta_thehive_cortex/libs/cortex4py/controllers/

# what the add-on actually calls
grep -rn "cortex\.\(jobs\|analyzers\|organizations\)\." \
     TA-thehive-cortex/package/bin --include=*.py | grep -v /libs/
```

⚠️ A gap is not automatically a defect -- plenty of methods have no business
here. It is a **question to answer once**, and the answer belongs in this file
if it is "no", like R44 above. What is not acceptable is never asking.
